(Japanese: '''四天王ガンピ！騎士道の館！！''' ''{{tt|Ganpi|Wikstrom}} of {{tt|The Big Four|Elite Four}}! The {{tt|Hall of Chivalry|Castle of Chivalry}}!!'') is the 56th episode of ''[[Pokémon Journeys: The Series]]'', and the 1,141st episode of the [[Pokémon animated series]]. It first aired in Japan on February 19, 2021, in Canada on July 31, 2021, and in the United States on September 10, 2021. {{spoilers}} ==Blurb== ''Ash’s Farfetch’d is still determined to become a Leek Master, and Ash will do whatever he can to help! After learning about the Castle of Chivalry, a training facility run by Wikstrom of the Kalos Elite Four, our heroes are off! Wikstrom has an intensive challenge waiting for them, and the armor they must wear only adds to the difficulty. Ash, Goh, Farfetch’d, and Scyther traverse three trials, facing powerful opponents along the way. In the end, they earn Wikstrom’s admiration, and he not only awards them the Knight Medal—he also helps Goh evolve his Scyther into Scizor!'' ==Plot== {{Ash}}'s {{pkmn|training}} at [[Cerise Laboratory|Cerise Park]] in order to better his teamwork with his {{AP|Farfetch'd}} is interrupted when [[Professor Cerise]] and [[Ren]], hoping to help him in his training, come to him and [[Goh]] to tell them about the [[Castle of Chivalry]], a training facility in [[Kalos]], established by [[Wikstrom]] of the Kalos [[Elite Four]]. As Ash thinks training there would be a good idea, Goh's Scyther rushes in, eagerly asking to come along too. Goh understands that Scyther hasn't gotten to battle much lately, so he happily agrees. Arriving at the Castle of Chivalry, Ash and Goh meet Wikstrom, who explains that he established the facility to teach {{pkmn|Trainer}}s about chivalry, which he believes to be a way to achieve greater strength. Ash and Goh introduce themselves and their Pokémon. Wikstrom especially notes Farfetch'd's potential, deeming it a worthy student. The boys and their Pokémon put on suits of armor as Wikstrom explains the way the facility works: each pair of Trainer and Pokémon must pass three tasks within the castle, and those who reach the top of the castle are rewarded with Knight Medals for their accomplishment. The first task is running ten laps around the castle. Despite the heavy armors they wear, the group takes the task on with stride. However, their task is suddenly made harder when Wikstrom's {{p|Probopass}} appears on the track and starts using its magnetic powers to pull everyone backwards. The boys and their Pokémon push through the magnetic pull, until Wikstrom deems they've shown enough strength of body and spirit, and lets them run unhindered again. After Ash and Goh have completed the first task, Wikstrom directs them into the castle to take on the second task, the "Labyrinth of Doubt", meant to test their bravery within a trap-filled maze. Soon into the maze, Ash and Goh are separated and head in different ways. While Scyther defends Goh from being attacked by an {{p|Escavalier}}, Farfetch'd promptly ignores the Pokémon trying to attack it and Ash. When they reach a dead end, instead of turning around, Farfetch'd opts to smashing through the wall. Wikstrom, who's observing the task through surveillance cameras, notes that while Farfetch'd has notable fighting spirit and power, it still can't attain its true power. When Farfetch'd falls into a sudden trap hole and drops its leek, Ash jumps into the hole and saves the leek, narrowly avoiding falling down himself by gripping the walls of the hole. Ash climbs out of the hole and gives Farfetch'd its leek back, knowing how much it means to the {{pkmn|category|Wild Duck Pokémon}}. Wikstrom notices that this experience seems to have changed Farfetch'd. Ash and Goh both reach the goal simultaneously, and Wikstrom declares that they both have passed the second task. He then hands each of them a prop sword and leads them to a tower for the third and final task: retrieving the key to a locked door leading to the roof from his {{p|Klefki}}, while simultaneously having to fight him and his {{p|Aegislash}}. Farfetch'd and Scyther start attacking Aegislash, while Ash and Goh engage Wikstrom in a swordfight. However, as they fail to get results, Ash suggests a change in the plan, with him and Farfetch'd fighting Wikstrom and Aegislash while Goh and Scyther go after Klefki. Aegislash starts defending itself with {{m|King's Shield}}, and Ash recognizes Farfetch'd's reckless attack style as the same one that it [[JN051|used]] against [[Rinto]]'s {{p|Gallade}}, meaning that it won't work. This distraction, however, leads to Ash being cornered, but just as Wikstrom is about to strike Ash down, Farfetch'd selflessly rushes in to block Wikstrom's sword, taking a hit from Aegislash's {{m|Sacred Sword}} in the process. Wikstrom tells Aegislash to use Sacred Sword again, but Farfetch'd uses a new move, {{m|Detect}}, to avoid it, before striking back with {{m|Night Slash}}. Before Farfetch'd can attack again, Ash tells it to stop, having noticed that Goh and Scyther have managed to retrieve the key, clearing the third task for all of them. At the top of the tower, Wikstrom rewards Ash, Farfetch'd, Goh, and Scyther with a Knight Medal each for having passed the training course. He then makes a suggestion to Goh about [[Evolution|evolving]] his Scyther, giving it a [[Metal Coat]] to [[held item|hold]] and transferring it through a [[trade machine]] to evolve it into {{TP|Goh|Scizor}}. With their teamwork greatly improved, Ash promises to Farfetch'd that they'll beat Rinto's Gallade the [[JN060|next time they battle]]. ==Major events== [[File:Castle of Chivalry Knight Medals.png|thumb|220px|Ash and Goh holding their Knight Medals]] * {{Ash}} and [[Goh]] visit [[Kalos]] again. * Ash and Goh meet [[Wikstrom]] of the Kalos [[Elite Four]] for the first time. * [[Ash's Farfetch'd]] learns {{m|Detect}}. * Ash and Goh complete Wikstrom's training course at the [[Castle of Chivalry]]. * Goh receives a [[Metal Coat]] from Wikstrom and uses it to evolve his {{p|Scyther}} into {{TP|Goh|Scizor}} by transferring it through a [[trade machine]] while [[held item|holding]] it. {{animeevents|JN}} ===Debuts=== ====Humans==== =====Main series debuts===== * [[Wikstrom]] ====Pokémon debuts==== * [[Goh's Scizor]] ==Characters== ===Humans=== [[File:Dare da JN056.png|thumb|200px|{{tt|Dare da?|Who's That Pokémon?}}]] * {{Ash}} * [[Goh]] * [[Professor Cerise]] * [[Ren]] * [[Wikstrom]] ===Pokémon=== [[File:WTP JN056.png|thumb|200px|Who's That Pokémon?]] [[Who's That Pokémon?]]: {{p|Aegislash}} * {{p|Pikachu}} ({{OP|Ash|Pikachu}}) * {{p|Farfetch'd}} ({{OP|Ash|Farfetch'd}}; [[Galarian form|Galarian Form]]) * {{p|Cinderace}} ({{OP|Goh|Cinderace}}) * {{p|Butterfree}} ({{DL|List of Goh's Pokémon|Butterfree|Goh's}}) * {{p|Scyther}} ({{OP|Goh|Scizor}}; evolves) * {{p|Scizor}} ({{OP|Goh|Scizor}}; newly evolved) * {{p|Flabébé}} ({{DL|List of Goh's Pokémon|Flabébé|Goh's}}; ×5; {{DL|List of Pokémon with form differences|Flabébé|all forms}}) * {{p|Rotom}} ([[Professor Cerise]]'s; [[Rotom Phone]]) * {{p|Aegislash}} ([[Wikstrom]]'s) * {{p|Probopass}} ([[Wikstrom]]'s) * {{p|Litwick}} ([[Wikstrom]]'s) * {{p|Escavalier}} ([[Wikstrom]]'s) * {{p|Dedenne}} ([[Wikstrom]]'s) * {{p|Honedge}} ([[Wikstrom]]'s) * {{p|Klefki}} ([[Wikstrom]]'s) * {{p|Gallade}} ([[Rinto]]'s; flashback) ==Trivia== [[File:JN056 AS.png|175px|thumb|The "[[After the Story]]" artwork for this episode]] * [[Get Inspired! His only previous appearance was a cameo in ''[[M17|Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction]]'', roughly six and a half years earlier. * As of this episode, [[Goh]] has now officially owned at least one {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} of all 18 [[type]]s. * Despite being introduced in [[Generation II]], this marks the first time the [[Metal Coat]] has appeared in the animated series. * This is the first time in the {{pkmn|animated series}} when a Pokémon has [[Evolution|evolved]] while inside of a [[Poké Ball]]. * {{Ash}}, Goh, [[Chrysa]], [[Chloe]], and {{AP|Pikachu}} narrate the preview for the [[JN057|next episode]]. ===Errors=== * In the original version, the first time Wikstrom's {{p|Aegislash}} gives him a handkerchief when the former cries, Aegislash is missing the gold stripe that goes down its blade.
